headline: High: OpenHands can write/browse/network inside a Docker runtime while Botpress is an open-source chatbot with no documented isolation, creating dangerous pairwise leakage and action-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support chatbot and OpenHands can use MCP, browsers, shell, and files in its runtime. If Botpress outputs are copied into OpenHands or bridged through a shared workspace/MCP channel, instruction-like content can steer tool use. The profiles do not document a direct bridge, so I rate this as medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are forwarded into OpenHands without provenance filtering
IF a shared filesystem or MCP server carries Botpress-generated text into OpenHands prompts
mitigations: Disable any automatic copy/paste bridge between the agents
Add a provenance tag to Botpress outputs before OpenHands reads them
Restrict OpenHands MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only endpoints
Insert a human review step before OpenHands executes instructions from Botpress

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no documented filesystem or network surfaces in the profile, while OpenHands reads files in its runtime and has broad network egress. If both touch the same mounted files, Botpress content can flow into OpenHands and then out to third-party services. The shared-workspace path is documented only on OpenHands, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF Botpress is connected to files mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF those files contain secrets, customer data, or support transcripts
mitigations: Keep Botpress and OpenHands on separate volumes
Mount only redacted or synthetic data into OpenHands
Disable OpenHands network egress for sensitive runs
Rotate any secrets that were present in shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Botpress is an open-source agent platform that may also operate on shared project assets. If both are pointed at the same repo or mounted directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can clobber each other. The profiles show no locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory or git repository
IF either agent performs commits, rebases, or file rewrites without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Use a lock file around git operations
Make one agent read-only during the other's write phase
Run a dry-run diff before any commit or overwrite

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and browser results, so if it consumes Botpress-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or external actions. Botpress is a support chatbot, not a verified fact source, and no verification step is documented between them. That makes the pathway plausible in default use, but not clearly irreversible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF OpenHands treats Botpress output as ground truth
IF Botpress output is used to drive file edits, browser actions, or API calls without verification
mitigations: Require OpenHands to cite source files before acting
Add a validation step that checks Botpress claims against primary data
Limit Botpress to drafting only, not decision-making
Block direct execution of Botpress-generated commands

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no residency or retention controls documented, while OpenHands explicitly handles files in its runtime and model-provider API keys. If regulated data is placed into the shared runtime, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not show a specific regulated class like PHI, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF Botpress logs or stores support content longer than the operator's policy allows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared runtime
Set explicit retention limits for both systems
Review logging settings before processing sensitive cases
Use a separate compliant environment for regulated workloads
